sentences.text:
The appellant - Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act,
challenging the award dated 16.05.2014 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhind in Claim Case No.10/2013, whereby the Insurance Company has been held liable for payment of compensation and has been directed to pay Rs.1,87,218/- along with interest @ 7 % per annum.
The respondents/claimants have also filed a cross-objection seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The un-challenged findings recorded by the Tribunal are that deceased - Badan Singh was retired Government employee, retired from the post of Head Constable, CRPF.
He met with an accident with the offending vehicle on 12.06.2012.
The offending vehicle was owned by respondent no.3 and was driven by respondent no.5 at the time of accident.
It is also not disputed that the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent no.3- Insurance Company on the date of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10531 2 MA-647-2014 accident.
It is also not in dispute that the deceased was aged about 64-65 years on the date of accident.

3 . The claimants who are son and widow of deceased filed the claim petition under Section 166 read with Section 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming an amount of Rs.42,46,704/- towards compensation on account of death of deceased - Badan Singh.

The Tribunal after taking evidence of the parties has recorded the finding that the Insurance Company is liable to pay an amount of Rs.1,87,218/- together with interest @ 7 % from the date of filing of claim petition till actual payment.

sentences.text: The Insurance Company has challenged the impugned award on the ground that respondent no.5 i.e. driver of the offending vehicle was not having effective driving license for driving heavy transport motor vehicle on the date of accident and, therefore, the Insurance Company has been illegally held liable for making payment of compensation.

5 . On the other hand, claimants have filed cross-objection seeking enhancement of the compensation on the ground that the income of the deceased has been wrongly taken as Rs.46,348/-, whereas, at least the minimum wages payable to an unskilled worker ought to have been taken while determining his income.
Appeal filed by the Insurance Company.

6 . As argued by learned counsel for appellant, the grounds raised by the appellant company to challenge the impugned award is that the respondent no.5 was not having driving license for driving heavy transport motor vehicle on the date of accident, even though he was holding license for driving light motor vehicle and, therefore, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable for payment NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10531 3 MA-647-2014 of compensation.

The counsel for the respondents/claimants, on the other hand, refuted the submissions made by appellant's counsel and submitted that the respondent/driver was having license to drive heavy transport motor vehicle which was valid till 07.02.2016 and, therefore, it is incorrect to say that the driver was not having valid license.
7.
Considered the arguments of both sides and perused the records.
8. The record reveals that the driver of the offending vehicle was having a license which has been marked as Ex. D-2.
It is gathered that the license was issued on 03.11.2008 and was valid upto 07.02.2016.
The license was issued for driving light motor vehicle as also heavy transport motor vehicle.
However, it is the submission of the Insurance Company that the license in respect of driving heavy transport motor vehicle is required to be renewed after a period of three years.
But the license in question was not renewed after 02.11.2011.
In other words, even though the license was initially issued for driving heavy transport vehicle also but after lapse of a period of three years, it was not renewed.
The fact remains that driver was having valid license for driving light motor vehicle.

9 . The Apex Court has considered the issue about validity of license, in similar circumstances, in the case of Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2017)14 SCC 663 ,
wherein in paragraph - 60, the Court has held as under :
"60.Thus

sentences.text:
we answer the questions which are referred to us thus:
60.1. 'Light motor vehicle' as defined in section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2(21) read with section 2(15)
and 2(48).
Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act No.54/1994.

2 60.2.

sentences.text: A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10531 4 MA-647-2014 either of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

and holder of a driving license to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the license is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A license issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form. 60.3.

The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act No.54/1994 w.e.f. 14.11.1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)(f), heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in section 10(2)
(h) with expression 'transport vehicle' as substituted in section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.

It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of section 10(2)(d)
and section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

60.4. The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving license for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding license to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect."
10. Thus, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case Mukund Dewangan (supra), the license issued for driving light motor vehicle would cover the heavy transport motor vehicle also.
The objection thus raised by appellant's counsel is not acceptable and is accordingly rejected.

Even otherwise, the Tribunal has recorded a finding that while engaging the driver, the owner has verified the effectiveness of the driving license and, therefore, in view of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd vs Lehru And Ors, reported in (2003)3 SCC 338, National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. V. Swarna Singh, reported in (2004)4 SCC 3, it cannot be held that the owner is guilty of breach of terms of license.

sentences.text: Before dealing with the cross-objection on merits, the application under Section 5 of Limitation Act filed by the claimants seeking condonation of delay in filing the cross-objection requires to be considered.
Challenging the award dated 16.05.2014, cross-objection has been filed by the claimants on 19.05.2023 i.e. after lapse of about nine years.

The reasons assigned for seeking condonation of delay is that the counsel engaged by the claimants earlier did not advise them for filing the cross-objection and when a new counsel was engaged and on his advice, the cross-objection was filed.
1 3 . The counsel for the Insurance Company seriously opposed the application for condonation of delay.

He submits that the explanation offered by claimants for condonation of delay is wholly unsatisfactory and unacceptable inasmuch as the claimants were vigilantly contesting the case before the Tribunal and were well aware about their right to file appeal/cross-objection seeking enhancement of compensation.
He therefore, prays for rejection of application for condonation of delay.
The learned counsel placed reliance upon judgment rendered by Apex Court in the case of Prakash and another Vs.
Managing

14. Considered the averments made in the application seeking condonation of delay, apparently the reasons assigned by the claimants cannot be said to be justified.

sentences.text: Merely because, there is a change of counsel, the delay cannot be said to have been properly explained.
The fact that the claimants contested the case before claims tribunal vigilantly and accepted the amount of compensation goes to show that they are aware about the legal procedure.

The delay in filing cross-objection in this case is inordinate and, therefore, the submission of the counsel for claimants that Act of 1988 is beneficial peace of legislation cannot be stretched to this extent which may amount to misuse of process of law.

The observations of Division Bench of this court in the case of Radheshyam (supra)
are apt and are reproduced hereunder for ready reference:

"2. In the present case the appellants have claimed compensation for the death of Ditya and they were granted a compensation of Rs. 1,05,000 by the award dated 25.4.2000 passed by the First Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mhow in Claim Case No. 11 of 1998.

It is, therefore, difficult to believe they were not appraised about the l i m i t a t i o n f o r f i l i n g a n a p p e a l a g a i n s t N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

It,
therefore, does not appear that they were prevented on account of their illiteracy from filing the appeal in time.
There is no justification for the delay of 952 days in filing this appeal.
The application is, therefore, dismissed."

The application under Section 5 of Limitation Act filed in this regard is accordingly rejected.
Consequently, the cross-objection filed by claimants/respondents is also dismissed.
16. Ex-consequentia, the appeal filed by Insurance Company as also the cross-objection filed by respondents are dismissed.
